documents.title: Responsible AI Use at UCF: Ethical Guidelines
documents.summary: UCF's AI for All initiative lists ethical guidelines: disclosure of AI use, no uploading of copyrighted material, vetting for deepfakes and hallucinations, and separate rules for students, faculty teaching and research, and staff. Whether students may use AI is left to each syllabus; faculty are told to avoid detectors and not to grade by AI alone.
documents.stance_why: The page says there is 'not, as yet, a Policy specifically about artificial intelligence' and tells students to 'look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted', so it sets disclosure and ethics expectations but leaves the permit-or-ban decision to courses.

units.why: The passage says intentional AI use 'must be disclosed' with an example citation, a university-wide duty on all users, so it is a disclosure rule (P24). The example includes tool, data-protection version and date, but the rule itself is disclosure, so P24 not P25.
units.anchor: AI-assisted tools for any element of a work or school product must be disclosed

units.why: The example 'an outline of topics for this work were generated by Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection, March 7, 2025' shows the disclosure should name the tool and date, which is what P25 covers.
units.anchor: generated by Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection, March 7, 2025
units.policy: The example disclosure names the tool (Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection), what it generated (an outline of topics) and the date
units.fit_note: Offered as an example, not a stated requirement to include prompt or output.

units.why: Says embedded AI such as 'predictive text sentence completions, auto-correct, spell check' 'does not need to be disclosed', a carve-out for routine features, matching P100 rather than P24 because it relaxes the rule.
units.anchor: does not need to be disclosed
units.frag_start: Use of AI that is embedded
units.frag_end: spell check, etc.), does not need to be disclosed
units.fit_note: Exemption is from disclosure, not from a ban.

units.why: States grammar-assistance disclosure is 'not centrally mandated for students' but 'may depend on individual faculty policy', which hands the grammar-help decision to instructors (P04) and concerns prose (P18); P04 chosen because the point is who decides.
units.anchor: not centrally mandated for students, but may depend on individual faculty policy
units.fit_note: Specific to disclosure of grammar assistance.

units.why: Says uploading copyrighted materials, including 'student assignments, publisher materials', to a tool that trains on or stores them 'is a copyright violation', forbidding uploads of protected works: P49.
units.anchor: It is a copyright violation to upload intellectual property / copyrighted materials
units.fit_note: Framed as a copyright violation and limited to tools that train or store; also covers library downloads.

units.why: Explains that 'Most AI tools use queries, uploads, and outputs to help train and refine their models', a factual statement of how tools handle data, so it informs about privacy (P50).
units.anchor: Most AI tools use queries, uploads, and outputs to help train and refine their models

units.why: Flags 'resources/money needed for some advanced AI tools, or the energy requirements' as matters needing attention, an equity-cost and environmental concern; environmental/ethical is the closer fit (P53), cost/access (P51) is not a requirement here.
units.anchor: the energy requirements of AI tools
units.fit_note: Also mentions money needed for advanced tools (access/equity, P51).

units.why: Says deepfakes and hallucinations 'must not be used fraudulently' and everyone must 'vet content', banning deceptive use (P74); the vetting duty is secondary, so P74 not P31.
units.anchor: must not be used fraudulently
units.frag_start: AI tools can be used to deceive
units.fit_note: Also includes duty to vet content and not transmit deepfakes.

units.why: States 'All people bear responsibility to vet content', requiring users to verify AI output and not circulate deepfakes; this is verification (P31).
units.anchor: All people bear responsibility to vet content
units.fit_note: Aimed at deepfakes and hallucinations, with a duty not to transmit or perpetuate them.

units.why: Says UCF has 'not, as yet, a Policy specifically about artificial intelligence', acknowledging no formal AI policy yet; nothing in the type list covers stating that no policy exists.
units.anchor: There is not, as yet, a Policy specifically about artificial intelligence.
units.uncovered_note: States that UCF has no university policy specifically on AI and points to a page of internal policies instead.

units.why: Notes that there are 'no statewide guidelines or mandates' in Florida and that federal law is not yet passed, describing the external legal landscape; it informs about laws (P77).
units.anchor: There are, as yet, no statewide guidelines or mandates for AI use or non-use.
units.fit_note: Says no state or federal law applies yet rather than requiring compliance.

units.why: Quotes the FAA rule that personnel 'must not use GAI to perform or facilitate illegal or malicious activities' and says UCF stakeholders are 'likely bound' as an FAA contractor, an external-rule compliance statement (P77).
units.anchor: As a contractor of the FAA, UCF stakeholders are likely bound by these guidelines.
units.fit_note: Compliance runs through a contractor relationship with the FAA and is stated as 'likely'.

units.why: Tells students to 'look to individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted', so the rule is set per course and students must find it: P78 (the student duty) rather than P04.
units.anchor: individual syllabi for guidance on how, when, and if AI use is permitted.

units.why: Says 'If no policy is stated, students should seek clarification from the instructor rather than make assumptions', which is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: students should seek clarification from the instructor rather than make assumptions about acceptable use

units.why: 'Students are responsible for the accuracy of the work they submit, whether AI assistance was employed or not' makes students answerable for submitted work: P29.
units.anchor: responsible for the accuracy of the work they submit, whether AI assistance was employed

units.why: 'Students who fraudulently represent AI output as their work are committing plagiarism' classes undisclosed AI-as-own work as plagiarism, i.e. misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Students who fraudulently represent AI output as their work are committing plagiarism.

units.why: Advises AI as 'a way to complement students' creativity' but 'not a replacement for their own critical thinking', i.e. students remain the thinker: P32.
units.anchor: not a replacement for their own critical thinking
units.frag_start: AI should be considered as a way
units.policy: AI should complement students' creativity and intellectual capabilities but not replace their own critical thinking; the most effective approach positions AI as a thought partner

units.why: Says the 'developmental journey' of researching, analyzing and articulating 'cannot be skipped without compromising the learning objectives', explaining that skipping the process harms learning (P41).
units.anchor: cannot be skipped without compromising the learning objectives
units.frag_start: Many faculty design writing and critical

units.why: Points to a further page of advice for students, a pointer to guidance rather than a rule; no type fits mere signposting, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: for additional advice for students considering AI use at UCF.
units.uncovered_note: Points students to a separate page of advice on AI use.

units.why: States faculty AI use for teaching 'must' be 'ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed', a faculty requirement including disclosure of their own AI use (P47).
units.anchor: use of AI for teaching is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed.
units.fit_note: Also requires ethical, responsible and fair use; disclosure audience not named.

units.why: 'Grading accomplished only through AI, with no human review, is not ethical and should be avoided' insists on human review of grading; P46 (humans assign grades), with P101 not chosen since no conditions are listed.
units.anchor: Grading accomplished only through AI, with no human review, is not ethical
units.fit_note: Bans AI-only grading, not AI-assisted grading.

units.why: Faculty are 'advised to avoid using AI detectors' because they are 'not reliable' and give false positives, which is P39.
units.anchor: Faculty are advised to avoid using AI detectors.

units.why: Says students writing in a non-native language 'are disproportionately likely to be unjustly accused of AI use', naming a bias harm of detectors, closest to P53, while the detector advice itself is P39.
units.anchor: writing in a non-native language are disproportionately likely to be unjustly accused of AI use
units.fit_note: Harm is unfair accusation of non-native writers via detectors.

units.why: Faculty 'may want to consider assignments that encourage student AI use as part of the learning process', a suggestion to design assignments around AI (P35).
units.anchor: faculty may want to consider assignments that encourage student AI use
units.frag_start: Because AI is now part of
units.fit_note: Suggestion to design assignments encouraging AI use; not a requirement.

units.why: States 'Recommendation letters produced solely by AI lack the personal insights', discouraging AI-only letters, which is instructor use of AI for teaching-related work (P59).
units.anchor: Recommendation letters produced solely by AI lack the personal insights
units.fit_note: Stated as a fact about quality, implying letters should not be AI-only.

units.why: Faculty AI use for research must also be 'ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed', a research-use rule (P62).
units.anchor: use of AI for research is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed.

units.why: Tells faculty to 'check with individual publishers regarding policies of AI use and/or disclosure', deferring to venue rules (P62).
units.anchor: Faculty should check with individual publishers regarding policies of AI use and/or disclosure.
units.frag_start: The potential use of AI tools

units.why: Says AI use for grant-writing 'is not universally accepted' and needs 'case-by-case decisions', a research rule of deferring to funder preferences (P62).
units.anchor: faculty will need to make case-by-case decisions
units.frag_start: Similarly, the use of AI tools

units.why: Notes some funders and publishers 'prohibit the use of AI when writing critiques, reviews', and faculty 'should seek clarification', deferring to external rules (P62).
units.anchor: Faculty should seek clarification about whether AI tools are permitted on a case-by-case basis.

units.why: Researchers must protect research data and use AI to analyze it 'only via enterprise-level platform access', a data-protection rule favoring vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: only via enterprise-level platform access to ensure data integrity and data security
units.frag_start: Researchers are responsible for the protection

units.why: 'For scholarly reviews, researchers should avoid using AI' because human judgment is essential, a research and peer review rule (P62).
units.anchor: For scholarly reviews, researchers should avoid using AI.

units.why: Staff and administrators must also use AI in ways that are 'ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed', which governs operational staff use (P76).
units.anchor: administrators must ensure their use of AI is ethical, responsible, fair, transparent, and disclosed.

units.why: Staff 'must be extra vigilant not to expose proprietary data, student records' to unsecured AI and should de-identify data, a data protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: not to expose proprietary data, student records, and other sensitive information to unsecured AI
units.frag_start: Staff have access to sensitive University
units.fit_note: Also prefers de-identification even within Copilot.

units.why: States the principles 'were developed and written without AI assistance' and lists groups who fine-tuned them, describing how the guidance was made (P84).
units.anchor: Groups that assisted in fine-tuning these principles include UCF IT

documents.title: Ethical Use of AI (students)
documents.summary: A student-facing page that mixes encouragement (AI fluency for careers, official Copilot-Chat with data protection) with a default that AI be avoided unless an instructor permits it. It stresses checking the syllabus, verifying output, and owning AI errors.
documents.stance_why: It says AI 'should be avoided unless explicitly permitted by the instructor', which makes permission the exception, although the page is otherwise warm about AI fluency and recommends Copilot-Chat; the avoid-unless-permitted line is the only operative default, so restrict.

units.why: States AI offers 'enormous opportunities' and that 'Students must embrace the inevitable changes, and... become proficient users of AI to remain competitive in the workplace', a career-skill rationale for AI (P44) with an expectation of use.
units.anchor: become proficient users of AI to remain competitive in the workplace
units.frag_start: AI presents enormous opportunities, as well

units.why: The quoted line 'the person who knows how to use AI will replace you' is a career-pressure framing for learning AI, so P44.
units.anchor: But the person who knows
units.frag_start: You may have heard it before
units.policy: The person who knows how to use AI will replace you
units.fit_note: Rhetorical quote used to motivate AI skill-building.

units.why: Calls Copilot-Chat 'the official AI tool at UCF' and recommends it, a university-sanctioned tool, so P92 (institution-wide licensed tool) rather than P17 (course-specific).
units.anchor: The official AI tool at UCF is Copilot-Chat
units.frag_start: The official AI tool at UCF

units.why: Explains that Copilot with Commercial Protection is a 'walled garden' where data 'stays local' and 'is NOT uploaded to Microsoft', a data-privacy assurance for the vetted tool (P50).

units.why: Says users should see a green shield showing 'data protection' mode, instructions for confirming use of the vetted tool safely (P50).
units.anchor: You should see a checkmark in a green shield near the top
units.policy: You should see a checkmark in a green shield near the top; this is how you know you are in data protection mode
units.fit_note: Procedural step for confirming the protected version.

units.why: Mentions a 'local copy is kept in a hidden (local) mailbox folder' under retention policies, a data-handling fact (P50).

units.why: 'its use should be avoided unless explicitly permitted by the instructor' is a fallback default: AI avoided unless permitted (P06), softer than a ban but the exception is instructor permission.

Several units (career planning, AI portfolio, pointer to advice page, no-policy statement) were coded UNCOVERED.
